Chapter one · 2019–2022
Degree
BA Motion Arts
School
AFDA, Johannesburg

Learning to build a frame

It started with the image.

At AFDA in Johannesburg I studied Motion Arts and specialised in VFX. The course taught me that a frame is constructed: light, layers, timing, and a hundred small decisions that nobody notices when they are right. I still work that way. Whether the thing in front of me is a film, a garment or a campaign, I look for the decisions underneath it.

Campaign
Ever changing play

Johannesburg

Play with an engineering spine

Then a brand that is built, quite literally, from parts.

In December 2022 I joined LEGO as a brand ambassador for the Ever changing play campaign, and I led the technology team. LEGO is a company where imagination has to survive manufacturing: every idea ends up as a piece that clicks into another piece. Leading the technology side of that campaign was the first time my two interests, art and engineering, had the same job.

A house of my own

TwoHoursPastCurfew, shortened to THPC.

I co-founded THPC and I lead it as executive creative director, which means the clothing, the imagery and the ideas behind them are decided in one room. It taught me the part of creative work that school cannot: an idea has to survive being made, worn and seen by strangers. Everything that follows in this chapter happened under that name.

3.1 · Performance
Format
Performance art piece
House
THPC
Film
Recap video, Cape Town

Voyagers’ Dream

Leaving the rail, entering the room.

Voyagers’ Dream is a performance piece made under THPC and documented in a recap film shot in Cape Town. It shows the house working at the scale of an installation, where the subject is a feeling and the clothes are only part of the set.

The thinking cap and Guapdad 4000

Sometimes the campaign finds you at a festival.

In 2022 Guapdad 4000 was in South Africa for Rocking the Daisies, and we met up. THPC was running its ADHD campaign for Mental Health Awareness Month, built around the thinking cap. He took the cap into his music video, which put the campaign’s message in front of his audience. The clip below is from that film.

In print

The work left the screen.

Between September 2023 and August 2024 the work appeared in four magazines, from Milan to Australia to GQ South Africa. Print is a different test. Nobody can scrub, zoom or skip, so the image has to hold up as one still thing on a page.

  • GMARO MagazineSeptember 2023
  • 6X Magazine, MilanSeptember 2023
  • InFrame Magazine, AustraliaSeptember 2023

A different audience

Same craft, new room.

In 2025 I spent four months as a junior marketing manager at Guud Global, a company that says it understands mobility. Much of what I made served the healthcare service industry, so the brief moved between film-style content and practical material written for doctors. It confirmed something I suspected: the discipline behind a good image carries into a clinic as well as it does onto a stage.
